column1: # The deviation census for Goal B (PAIRS.md sec.1).
# One row per documented deviation. Columns, tab separated:
#   line    the 1-based line in that file where the deviation's text begins
#   note    why it is that class, in one clause
# `visible`   a screenshot of the pair -- the window, its decorations and the
#             client area -- would differ. Includes differences that only appear
#             while an interaction is driven (the note says "interaction only").
# `invisible` both windows render identically; the difference is mechanism, an
#             unpainted id, stdout, or input behaviour that leaves the same
# `forced`    visible, and there is a proof it cannot be removed inside the
#             binding's ABI (a register row or an API-COVERAGE.md sec.3 entry).
# `scripts/pair-census.sh` checks this table against the examples themselves:
# every bullet in a deviation section that has no row here, and every row whose
# line does not begin a deviation, is reported.

column4: note
the row builder is reached through run_with_rows instead of cx.processor
upstream's quotes come from rand::rng(); there is no fixed target to match
the visible row range is obtained differently; the same rows are drawn
ui::list takes 22.0 as the row height, the port's reading of upstream's measured height
a Gossamer frame rebuilds the tree; every pixel is the same
the ghost is a tree element, not GPUI's drag-preview layer; gpui paints the preview after the root and the ghost is the root stack's last child, so the paint order matches
an invisible full-window on_mouse overlay restores the same behaviour
animate() keeps the ghost following; the same pixels
handlers are plain functions over the store; cx.listener has no equivalent
the image loads by path instead of through AssetSource; the same pixels
the image's id is unstable, so frames are requested continuously; frame 0 either way
a custom Asset with a Duration is unreachable (AX2); cells 2 and 3's 5s comes from the port's own gpui::task timer, and the subtrees are the same elements at the same times
both pulse from phase 0 on a 3s cycle; the sampled alpha can differ by a frame
the editor is Rust-side code; the shell it draws is the same
the thirteen keys are matched on the element instead of through the keymap; the same text results

the editor is a document editor -- it holds breaks and handles the keys that move by them, where upstream binds neither; DW1 plus ui::editor(key, placeholder, style) handing out the widget whole are the proof
focus is taken when the editor is created rather than at startup
the shell is reproduced, and Reset is upstream's own -- on_reset_click clears the keystroke log and resets the text too (input.rs:622-627)
interaction only: cmd-w is not wired; the desktop quit shortcut is bound instead
asset paths point at examples/assets/ rather than the crate's own examples/image/
every image carries a binding-allocated id, so the window repaints; frame 0 either way
no Entity graph, no subscription object, nothing for notify() to re-render -- PORTING.md sec.5
Change { increment: usize } becomes untyped payload text
cx.emit is flushed within the enclosing update, not delivered on a subscription
upstream's assert_eq! is silent or fatal; here it is a panel
the binding can only run a program through gpui::run, which opens a window
the button and the event log are the port's own additions
no line-join option; at 1px bevel and miter are indistinguishable
paths are rebuilt each frame; the strokes themselves are the same
a Gossamer frame rebuilds the tree; every pixel is the same
paths live in a persistent pool addressed by handle; the same 2000 are painted
gpui::animate() is window.request_animation_frame()
a Gossamer frame rebuilds the tree; every pixel is the same
the quit handler does not print; stdout, not pixels
the app is activated when the window opens instead of by the example
set_menus stores but shows no bar on Linux, which is upstream's behaviour there too
hsla is quantised to the nearest hex step
an El's style is fixed at build time; the shapes are the same
element ids belong to the binding, which allocates one per element
a Gossamer frame rebuilds the tree; the colours themselves are exact
a focusable box wraps a ui::button; the same pixels
ui::text(..) is the binding's div().child(text), the same two-level element
ui::styled_text wraps the StyledText in a div, the same nesting
a Gossamer frame rebuilds the tree; the tree itself is the same
the root div's id is not set; layout is unaffected
init_colors runs once at startup, which is what makes default_color work
the type scale is derived in f64; the difference is under a thousandth of a pixel
ui::panel is the bare div upstream uses
the character list is written already cut into rows
the scroll box's id is not set
a Gossamer frame rebuilds the tree; next_id has no counterpart
40 levels render where upstream renders 50
ui::list takes 22.0 explicitly, the port's reading of upstream's measured height
the builder is handed to run_with_rows instead of being uniform_list's argument
no display_id window option, so a window cannot be pinned to a display
GPUI's macOS Display::bounds() reports the origin as (0,0) for every display
gpui::run always opens a host window of its own; upstream opens none
the host window's view draws every window; they are told apart by window_id
the labels reproduce DisplayId's Debug through display_field
titlebar=none is asked for, so the titlebar the binding attaches is invisible
the host window's own size is explicit, as everywhere in these ports
the Decorations::Client arm cannot run on macOS
set_client_inset is not exposed and is a no-op on macOS
insert_hitbox / set_cursor_style / start_window_resize / start_window_move / show_window_menu are called only inside the dead arm, so no macOS frame differs
window.refresh() is not exposed; the platform asks for a frame
observe_window_appearance only called window.refresh()
stop_propagation has nothing to stop in the Server arm
element ids belong to the binding
the colours are exact -- a note, not a difference
div() becomes ui::rect / ui::panel / ...; a Gossamer frame rebuilds the tree
sub-windows are centred on the primary display, not placed by display id
both bar the same: gpui sets a title only for Some(title), and "" is empty either way (mac/window.rs:740)
titlebar=none moves the traffic lights into a 32px client-drawn bar
geometry is returned as scalars; the structs are declared in the program
events are process-wide; each sub-window is given its own close handler
an invisible sub-window keeps the program alive, so it does not quit with the visible ones
ui::button supplies its own flex / items=center / justify=center / cursor=pointer
